question.text: Consider three vectors $A=i+j-2 k,\mathbf{B}=\hat{\mathbf{i}}-\hat{\mathbf{j}}+\hat{\mathbf{k}} \text { and } \mathbf{C}=2 \hat{\mathbf{i}}-3 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+4 \hat{\mathbf{k}} . \text { A vector } \mathbf{X} \text { of }$ the form $\alpha A+\beta B(\alpha$ and $\beta$ are numbers) is perpendicular to C. The ratio of $\alpha$ and $\beta$ is

solution.text:
Vector $\mathrm{X}$ of the form $\alpha \mathrm{A}+\beta \mathrm{B}$
$\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{X} &=\alpha \mathrm{A}+\beta \mathrm{B} \\
&=\alpha(\hat{i}+\hat{j}-2 \hat{k})+\beta(\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k}) \\
X &=\hat{i}(\alpha+\beta)+\hat{j}(\alpha-\beta)+\hat{k}(-2 \alpha+\beta)
\end{aligned}$
A vector $\mathrm{X}$ is perpendicular to $\mathrm{C},$ i.e., $\mathrm{X} \cdot \mathrm{C}=0$
$\text {or } -9 \alpha+9 \beta=0 \text { or } \alpha=\beta$
or $\frac{\alpha}{\beta}=\frac{1}{1} \text { or } \alpha: \beta=1: 1$
